Category: Architecture.
Subject: Dutch windmill.
Style: Animal Crossing.

spec.name: Dutch Windmill (Animal Crossing)
spec.description: A chunky, pastel, storybook Dutch tower windmill with a gallery deck, a teal shingled cap, four striped cloth sails and a tail pole, built in an Animal Crossing toy-diorama style.
spec.layout:
STYLE: Animal Crossing. Everything is chunky, rounded and toy-like: thick trim, oversized round-topped windows and door, soft pastel flat colours, warm woods, no thin or fussy parts. Edges get fat lighter 'highlight' strips or darker 'outline' strips as small parts. Repeating motif: a small TULIP (three-petal red or yellow head on a green stem, with two leaves) plus a LEAF. It appears on the door, the sail cloth, the signboard, the cap boards and the planters.

COORDINATES: +Y up, front +Z, left +X, centred on x=0. All values are metres. The tower is an OCTAGONAL tapering prism with a FLAT FACE toward +Z, so faces point at yaw 0, 45, 90... degrees. Apothem = distance centre to flat face. Circumradius = apothem / 0.924. For a lathe with 8 segments, spin it 22.5 degrees so a flat face looks to +Z.

STACK FROM THE GROUND UP:
1) Stone plinth: octagon, apothem 3.3, y 0 to 1.0 (tower part).
2) Walls: apothem 3.0 at y=1.0 tapering linearly to 2.15 at y=8.6. Apothem(y) = 3.0 - 0.1118*(y-1). Cream plaster with a brick-red band at y 4.6-4.9 and a brick-red cornice at y 7.9-8.6 (tower part).
3) Gallery deck: octagon, apothem 3.7, slab y 2.2 to 2.5, railing at apothem 3.55 reaching y 3.5, corbel brackets under it, stairs up the +X side (gallery part).
4) Cap: round, rim radius 2.7 at y 8.6, onion-dome of teal shingles rising to a peak at y 11.6, gold finial and weathervane to y 12.5 (cap part). A nose housing covers the windshaft at the front, to z 3.2.
5) Windshaft and sails: horizontal axle along +Z at y=9.6 from z 2.6 to the hub at z 4.0. Four sails in an X pose at 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees from up. Each stock is 6.2 m long from the hub. The sail plane is z 4.0 to 4.3 and a spinner cone ends at z 4.9. The lowest sail tip is at y of about 4.6, well above the gallery railing, and the sails clear the tower.
6) Tail pole (staart): a ladder-like beam from the cap back at [0,9.0,-2.55] sloping down to the ground at [0,0.35,-6.6], with a capstan winch beside its foot (tail part).
7) Door yard: the arched door with its porch frame on the front face under the gallery deck, plus planters, barrels, sacks, a hanging lantern and a signboard (doorYard part).

FRONT TO BACK: sail plane z 4.0-4.3 and spinner to z 4.9, door yard z 2.9-4.6, gallery and tower (centred at z 0), cap, tail pole going back and down to z -7.0. Resting on the floor: plinth, stair bottoms, door yard props, tail pole foot and capstan.

SILHOUETTE: a squat, wide plump tower, a big round teal hat, huge cheerful sails with cream cloth and coral stripes. Windows are warm-glowing. The model reads like a cozy village landmark.

parts.builds: The octagonal body (flat face to +Z, dimensions as in layout). Stone plinth (plinthStone, y 0-1.0, apothem 3.3) with a plinthDark chamfer course on top and a few lighter stones as small parts. Tapering wallCream walls (apothem 3.0 at y 1.0 to 2.15 at y 8.6) built as a loft or a stack of frusta. Brick-red band (brick, with brickDark course lines and small brick blocks) at y 4.6-4.9. A brick cornice (brick, brickDark underside) at y 7.9-8.6. Fat trimWhite corner pilasters on all 8 edges, slightly proud of the walls. Soft wallShade horizontal plaster lines every ~0.9 m. The door porch on the front face: a trimWhite surround box x -0.85..0.85, y 0-2.15, z 2.9-3.5, with a doorTeal arched plank door in it (vertical plank lines in woodDark, a gold knob, a tulip emblem above the door in tulipRed with leaf leaves, a round little transom window). All of this stays below the gallery deck at y 2.2. Chunky round-topped windows (glass panes lit with glowWarm inside, trimWhite frame, doorTeal shutters on both sides, woodLight sill with a tiny tulip pot) at yaw 0 and +-45 degrees at y 5.7, at yaw +-90 degrees at y 4.3 and at yaw +-135 degrees at y 6.9. Also small round glass port-holes at y 7.3 on yaw 0 and 180. A back round window at yaw 180 at y 5.7. The walls at the top end in a trimWhite ring where the cap sits at y 8.6.
parts.attaches: Rides joint base. Gallery deck sits on mount galleryDeck (y 2.4) around its walls; the cap rests on towerTop/capRing; the door porch is at doorCenter.

parts.builds: The wraparound gallery (stage) at mount galleryDeck. Octagonal deck slab (woodWarm top, woodDark edge fascia, apothem 3.7, y 2.2-2.5) with plank seam lines as thin woodDark strips. Under it, 8 chunky angled corbel brackets (woodLight) going from the wall to the deck underside, one per face, plus a woodDark rim board. Railing at apothem 3.55: woodLight posts at every corner and midpoint, with a top rail (woodLight) at y 3.5 and a mid rail at y 3.0 (trimWhite). Leave a gap in the railing where the stairs land at the +X side. A turned finial ball on each corner post. Stairs on the +X side, x 3.6-5.0 and z -1.8 to 3.6, going up from the ground at mount galleryStairBottom (z 3.6, y 0) to the deck at galleryStairTop (z -1.2, y 2.4): 8 treads (woodWarm, rise 0.3, run 0.6) on two woodDark stringers, a landing platform at deck level, a handrail (woodLight) with posts along the outer side, and a hanging tulip-motif board (tulipRed tulip on a trimWhite plank) at the landing. Small iron lantern hooks at the deck underside, and two coils of rope hung on the railing in woodLight.
parts.attaches: Rides joint base. Deck centres on galleryDeck and wraps the tower walls (do not rebuild walls). The door porch sits beneath it, and door-yard props stay below y 2.2 in front. The deck leaves room for the cap above.

parts.builds: The turning cap (rides joint cap). A trimWhite and woodDark rim ring at y 8.6-8.9, radius 2.7. Above it, a round onion dome (lathe, 16 segments, radius 2.6 at the rim, up to a peak at y 11.6) clad in roofTeal shingles. Stack 6 rows of scalloped shingle bands (alternating roofTeal and roofTealDark) as flattened rings or half-discs seated on the dome. A gold ring at the peak with a gold acorn finial to y 12.2 and a weathervane to y 12.5: an iron rod, a gold arrow and a tiny tulipRed tulip cut-out. Two round gabled dormer windows at yaw +-70 degrees from front (glass glowing glowWarm, trimWhite frames, roofTealDark mini hoods), and one small hatch at the back. The front nose housing (woodWarm box, woodLight rounded front with a trimWhite collar, z 2.0-3.2, around the shaft at mount shaftBase y 9.6) blends into the dome. At the back, a woodDark beam stub and an iron bracket mark the tailRoot mount [0,9.0,-2.55]. Three small tulipRed/tulipYellow tulip emblems on trimWhite boards around the rim.
parts.attaches: Rides joint cap. Sits on the tower top at capRing/towerTop. The windshaft (sails part) enters the nose housing at shaftBase. The tail pole attaches at tailRoot.

parts.builds: The windshaft and four sails (rides joint sailHub, pivot at mount hub [0,9.6,4.0]). A woodDark axle along +Z from z 2.6 to the hub. A gold bearing collar at z 3.3. The hub: a chunky woodWarm cylinder disc, radius 0.5, z 3.85-4.35, with a trimWhite rim and 8 iron bolt dots. A rounded spinner nose cone in tulipRed, z 4.3-4.9, with a gold tip ball. Four identical sails at 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees from up (X pose), each built the same way: a main stock beam of woodWarm (square 0.2 section, 6.2 m long from the hub centre, centred at z 4.1) with a woodLight highlight stripe on it. A latticed frame offset toward the counter-clockwise side as seen from the front: woodLight outer rail 1.3 m from the stock, running r=1.0 to 6.0 along the stock, with 7 cross battens (woodLight) and a tip bar. A flat sailCloth panel (thin, z 4.12-4.18) filling the lattice cells from r=1.2 to 5.9, in three bands of cloth. Add sailStripe coral diagonal or horizontal stripes on every other cell, and one tulip motif (tulipRed head and leaf leaves) near the root of each sail. Cloth is slightly inset from the battens. A small iron tip cap at each stock end. Max extent is 5.2 m from the axis.
parts.attaches: Rides joint sailHub (the axle stub from z 2.6 to 3.7 also rides sailHub). It meets the cap nose housing at shaftBase. The sails clear the tower and gallery (lowest tip at y of about 4.6).

parts.builds: The tail pole (staart) at the back, riding joint cap. Two woodWarm rails (radius 0.12, x +-0.22) running from tailRoot [0,9.0,-2.55] down to tailFoot [0,0.35,-6.6], with woodLight rungs every ~0.7 m. At the top, an iron bracket and a woodDark yoke clamp onto the cap beam stub. About two thirds down, a diagonal woodDark brace and a hanging rope coil. At the foot, two short woodDark ground stakes with iron rings. At mount capstan [1.2,0,-6.4], a capstan winch: a woodWarm round post (height 1.1, radius 0.2) on a plinthStone round footing, a woodLight cap disc, four woodLight spokes with round knobs at y 0.95, and a rope (woodLight, tied toward the pole foot with a small sweep). A little trimWhite plate with a tiny tulip decal marks the capstan. A weathered feel using plinthDark stones around the footing.
parts.attaches: Rides joint cap (it swings with the cap). Top meets the cap at tailRoot. The foot and capstan rest on y 0 at tailFoot and capstan.

parts.builds: Cozy Animal Crossing-style props around the front door, all low, under the gallery deck (y < 2.2), z 2.9-4.6, centred on doorCenter. A flagstone path from the door to z 4.6 (plinthStone and plinthDark rounded slabs, set flush). A woodWarm doormat with a stripe. Two woodLight flower planters either side of the door (x of about +-2.0, y 0-0.7, with woodDark bands), each packed with 5-6 tulips (tulipRed, tulipYellow) and leaf-green leaves and stems. A cheerful fenced bed of tulips on each outer side, as small parts (leaf stems, tulip heads, cup shapes). Two barrels (woodWarm staves with iron hoops, x about -2.6, z 3.8) and a stack of 3 sacks (sack colour, with tied necks and brick patches, x about +2.8, z 3.7) plus a small wooden crate. A hanging lantern at mount lanternHook [1.3,2.2,3.5]: an iron bracket, a gold cap, a glowWarm glowing body, and a tulip cutout. A signboard on a post (woodLight board, woodDark post, a trimWhite panel with a tulipRed tulip, leaf-green leaves and tiny text-bar marks) at x about -1.5, z 4.1. A little bench on the right next to the door. A few tiny pebbles and grass tufts (leaf).
parts.attaches: Rides joint base. Rests on y 0 in front of the door (mount doorCenter) and the plinth. The lantern hangs from the gallery deck underside at lanternHook. Keep clear of the stairs on +X (x > 3.6).

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out a Dutch windmill design in Animal Crossing style, planning a base, rotating cap, and sail hub joint with alphanumeric naming, and starting to work out the overall dimensions.

Now I'm working through proportions: a tapered octagonal stone tower around 8 units tall with a gallery ring at y=3.2, a thatched cap from 8-9.8 with a tail pole extending back, and a hub mounted at (0, 8.6, 2.0) holding 6-unit sails that reach a total height near 14.6 and a span around 12.4 units wide.

I'm checking for collisions between the sail tips and the gallery railing, and adjusting the hub height and gallery position so the sails clear the railing with enough margin.

I'm settling on the shaft projecting slightly beyond the cap dome for a chunky, Animal Crossing-style proportion, with thick blades and a tall overall silhouette.

Let me recompute the sizing: tower body up to y=8.6, cap from 8.6–11, hub around y=9.8, giving sail bottom at 3.4 clearing the gallery railing, and top reaching roughly 16.3 overall height, with sail span near 13 wide in a plus-shaped cross orientation.

Actually I should decide the sail orientation — maybe an "X" at 45° looks more dynamic, giving tips at y=5.3 (clearing the gallery) and a width/height around 9.6–14.3. I'll settle on the "X" rest pose for a more iconic windmill look.

Now figuring overall bounding box: accounting for tail pole, sail plane, and gallery front, I land on a size around [9.8, 14.6, 11.2], centered at x=0.

For the part breakdown, I'm splitting the model into five pieces, starting with a foundation/tower part combining the plinth, brick tower body, door, windows, and steps.

Second part is the gallery and its surroundings — a deck with railing, support posts and brackets, a stairs/ladder down the side, hanging lantern, and a door awning, with floor set true since the stairs reach ground level.

Third part is the cap — the dome roof with thatch/shingle covering.

For the cap I'm also planning a windowed ring, finial, weathervane, back balcony, hub housing at the nose, wind shaft, and tail pole base mount. Then the sails joint needs a hub with four blades, each made of wooden stocks, lattice frames, and striped cloth panels with tip details. Finally for the tail section I'm including the tail pole with winch wheel and ladders down to the ground, plus small decorative touches like tulip beds, a wooden sign, and door-side planters, while skipping anything not explicitly named like a grass base platform.

I'm settling on five parts overall: tower, gallery, cap, sails, and a combined tail-and-decor piece covering the tail pole, winch, tulip planters, barrels, sacks, and lamp for balanced detail. For joints, I'm placing a root "base" joint near the origin with an upward spine direction, a "cap" joint higher up that hinges around the vertical axis for rotation, and a "sailHub" joint near the cap front where the shaft runs along Z as a hinge for the turning blades.

I'm now working out the mounting radii and taper of the octagonal tower structure — sizing the plinth base, the tapering walls up to the cap, and figuring where the gallery platform sits relative to those dimensions.

Checking the gallery deck size against the sail positions, I set the outer radius and railing height so the sails clear the structure properly, then move up to sizing the cap's base ring and dome height toward the hub mount point.

Now I'm working out the dome cap dimensions: radius tapering to a peak with a finial on top, plus the nose housing projecting forward and the back edge extent. Then I calculate the sail assembly dimensions from hub position and blade length, figuring out the overall bounding size needed to fit the blades, weathervane, and tips within the total height.

Next I'm placing the tail pole, running it from the back of the cap down to a sinking anchor point near the ground, checking the length works out, and adding a winch wheel partway down the pole with the anchor post set at the base.

Now I'm working out the color palette, leaning toward cream plaster walls with brick-red accents for a warm Dutch-mill feel, picking out tones for the plinth stone, wall bands, brick trim, and wood details.

Adding more palette colors...

Splitting the part budget across tower, gallery, cap, sails, and tailDecor to stay under the total limit, then working out the tower's box geometry and how the octagonal plinth and door should be oriented relative to the front face.

Now I'm working out how the walls taper from the plinth to the top, where the gallery deck and railing sit relative to the tapering walls, and how the door at ground level should align with the gallery deck above it so it reads as a canopy over the entrance.

No stairs at the door itself—stairs to the gallery are on the +X side instead. I'm placing windows on the tower walls at heights 4.2, 6.0, and 7.4 across several octagon faces, computing the apothem shrink with height, and sizing the gallery as a ring box with stairs extending down from its +X side to the floor.

I'm working out the stair dimensions: 8 steps with roughly 0.3 rise and 0.45-0.6 run, spanning from about z=3.6 down to z=-1.2, keeping width around 1.0 to 1.5m and positioning the box so it clears the sail geometry above.

Let me lay out the remaining boxes roughly: the gallery floor sits at ground level overlapping the tower. The cap gets its own box spanning up to the weathervane height, including side windows and a tailbeam mount with a small hatch door. The sails form a box centered around y=9.6 with roughly ±5.0 spread, plus a hub cone for the mounting point.

Now I'm defining the windshaft and hub, figuring out where sails attach versus the cap's nose cone, and working out blade geometry — four blades at 45° increments with a spar length and lattice sail frame offset on the trailing edge.

Then I'm shifting to decor placement, trying to decide whether the flowerboxes and planters go by the front door or near the tail/winch area, settling on a separate "doorYard" piece for planters, barrels, and sacks near the entrance.

I'll settle on six parts total — tower, gallery, cap, sails, tailPole, doorYard — with budgets summing to 840, and define the doorYard bounding box near the front entrance to hold planters, barrels, stacked sacks, and a hanging lantern without colliding with the sails.

For doorYard I'm also thinking through doormat, stepping stones, and small signage, while checking that the gallery's underside sits at y=2.2 and that its support brackets angle from the wall between y 1.5–2.2 — meaning doorYard props need to stay clear of that bracket zone near the wall.

Now I'm sketching out planters flanking the doorway at modest height, a hanging lantern tucked near the door frame, and then setting the floor flags confirming tower, gallery with stairs, and tailPole as active while cap and sails stay off. I'm starting to lay out the joint hierarchy, beginning with the base root and the cap joint hinging off it.

Next I'm adding the sail hub joint hinging off the cap, then mapping each part to its parent joints — tower and gallery to base, cap and sails to the cap/hub group, tailPole riding the cap, doorYard off base — and beginning to define key mount points like ground center, plinth top, door center, and gallery deck positions.

I'm also working out the door's front surface geometry, since the plinth and wall faces sit at slightly different z-depths as the wall tapers upward, and the door surround box needs to protrude a bit beyond both.

I'm sizing the door to fit under the deck slab (keeping the header below y 2.2), then planning the tower's windows—round-top glazed shutter pairs placed at three height bands around the faces—plus belt-ring trim and the overall plinth/stone color scheme.

For the wall coloring, I'm deciding between a brick-lower/cream-upper split versus all-cream plaster, eventually settling on brick-red cladding up to around y 4.6 with dark mortar course lines, transitioning to cream plaster with shading stripes above, trimmed with white timber beams.

Overall the aesthetic needs to stay chunky, rounded, pastel, and stylized with thick trim and oversized windows, in that cozy Animal Crossing style with warm tones, round-topped features, and leaf motifs woven throughout.

For the cap shape I'm settling on an onion-ish dome with scalloped teal shingle rows and lathe ring boards, topped with a cute gold acorn finial and a heart-shaped weathervane instead of anything too fussy.

Now I need to write the spec precisely enough that builders match conventions exactly, so I'm defining the octagonal prism orientation (flat face toward +Z, rotated 22.5° so faces land at yaw 0, 45, etc.) and working out the apothem-to-circumradius conversion so the plinth measurements stay consistent.

I'm laying out the actual numeric constants: plinth apothem 3.3 (circumradius 3.57) spanning y 0–1.0, walls tapering from apothem 3.0 at y1.0 down to 2.15 at y8.6 using a linear formula, a deck at apothem 3.7 with railing at 3.55 up to y3.5, and a round cap radius of 2.6.

Now I'm working out the roof dome details with 16-segment lathe geometry, cap ring dimensions, peak and finial heights up to y12.6, and the front-facing hub/nose housing with shaft and sail plane depths extending to about z4.9.

Calculating overall size: z extends from tail anchor at -7.0 to spinner at 4.9, giving roughly 11.9-12.0 total depth, so I'm settling on dimensions [10.2, 14.8, 12.0] with stairs and sail width checks fitting within ±5.1. I'm also confirming the hub sits properly within the cap dome at that height so the nose housing clears correctly.

Now I'm working out the sail blade geometry — checking tip extents at 45° angles against the overall body height and width limits to confirm the lateral offset toward the counter-clockwise side stays within bounds.

Adding the cloth panel with ladder-pattern stripes and spinner cone, then working out the tail pole structure as a ladder with rails, rungs, and a capstan winch wheel at the ground end, matching how real windmill tail poles are built.

Repositioning the capstan to avoid overlapping the pole foot, settling on a post at [1.2, 0, -6.4] with spokes and a coiled rope, and bounding the whole tail assembly in a box roughly ±1.8 wide and up to y=9.2.

Now I'm finalizing the overall budget at 840 and locking in the color palette of 23 hues — stones, creams, brick reds, warm woods, teal doors and roofing — while planning the tulip-and-leaf motif to repeat across the sail, cap boards, signboard, and door for visual cohesion.
